nyc_found: DHS daily report PDF, pulled today (9/3/2026, reflecting 9/2/2026 data): Total Individuals = 83,781.
match_found: World Bank API: Andorra population, 2025 = 82,904 (most recent year available; matches match_value exactly).
conflict: The DHS source is a live daily-updating PDF at a fixed URL with no date-stamped archive. Today it shows 83,781, not the 83,549 cited in the claim -- a difference of 232. The stated figure was very likely accurate on whatever day it was originally pulled, but the claim carries no as-of date and the source URL will never again display 83,549 for a reader to check against. This is a structural sourcing problem: the number is not independently verifiable from the cited link, only trending in the same range (the daily count has hovered between about 83,500 and 84,000 in recent data). The Andorra side is solid and current.
finding: The NYC figure cannot be verified against its own source because the source is a live daily report, not a fixed snapshot; the linked page today shows 83,781, about 0.3% higher than the 83,549 claimed. Recommend either adding an explicit as-of date to the claim or noting that DHS's daily count fluctuates day to day.

nyc_found: FRED series GDPALL36061, titled "Gross Domestic Product: All Industries in New York County, NY" (i.e., Manhattan only) -- 2024 value = $1,006,673,239 thousand ($1.007 trillion).
match_found: IMF Datamapper NGDPD API: Indonesia 2024 = $1,396.302 billion (matches match_value exactly).
derived: The cited nyc_value ($1,377,841,498,000) is not what the nyc_url displays. It is a sum of five separate FRED county-GDP series that were never individually cited: New York County/Manhattan (36061, $1,006,673,239K) + Bronx (36005, $58,323,409K) + Kings/Brooklyn (36047, $145,934,266K) + Queens (36081, $143,131,298K) + Richmond/Staten Island (36085, $23,779,286K) = $1,377,841,498K, exactly matching the claimed total. The arithmetic is correct, but the single URL given as the source only supports the Manhattan-only figure, about 27% of the true total.
finding: A reader who clicks the cited source sees Manhattan County's $1.007 trillion GDP, not the $1.38 trillion figure printed in the claim -- there is no way to verify the actual number from the link provided. The $1.38 trillion is a legitimate five-borough sum (the math checks out against all five FRED county series), but it is an undisclosed derived total: no caveat says so, and the URL points to only one-fifth of the underlying data. This should either link to all five series or state outright that the figure sums Bronx, Kings, New York, Queens and Richmond counties.

Swapping in the 2026 figure would turn a near-even comparison (ratio 1.0175) into NYC schools spending clearly less than Iceland's economy (ratio would become roughly 1.155), which changes the rhetorical thrust of the claim more than any other item in this batch. Since NYC's FY2027 budget spans July 2026-June 2027, the 2026 estimate is arguably the more contemporaneous figure, though it remains an IMF projection rather than settled GDP.
finding: Both cited figures confirmed exactly as stated, correctly framed as a spending proposal versus a national economy. Flagging the Iceland GDP vintage as the one instance in this batch where choosing a different (equally defensible) year from the same IMF source would materially change how close the comparison reads.
